observed: Plan review, no blocking finding. Relaxing _read_owner from [st_dev, st_ino] equality to storage_identity.compare_identity does not create a credible deletion of non-owned content. The path is bound by the pinned O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY walk from the configured root (_parent/_target) and by the recorded repository and wave fields. Deletion also needs the 128-bit random generation to equal the lifecycle-captured expected_generation, re-checked by verify() before every unlink and rmdir. So a replacement directory that reuses the inode, a different repository at the same path, or a same-filesystem bind mount is accepted only if it holds a copy of the original .owner.json, which makes it a copy of the disposable work area itself. Planting or copying that file needs write access under the repository, which is the operator's own authority (threat model: same-user actors are trusted or out of scope), and anyone with that access could delete the files directly, so an attacker gains nothing. Link swaps are unaffected: _parent, _entry and _anchor stay strict on device and inode within one operation (Requirement 3). _empty_directory lstats each entry with follow_symlinks=False and unlinks links as entries without opening them. It opens subdirectories with O_NOFOLLOW, compares them with _same against their lstat, refuses a different device per child (work_filesystem_changed), and re-verifies identity per entry before each unlink or rmdir. None of this changes. The Risks row on inode reuse is honest but understated: the generation match is the strongest mitigation and should be named as such. Non-blocking notes: (1) Probed: compare_identity returns matches:true, basis:'path' when either inode is 0, so a stored [dev, 0] would accept any directory at the path. Only a same-user edit of the owner file can produce that, and the file lives inside the directory it guards. Recommend the implementation also refuse a zero inode, or AC-3 cover it, because this check gates deletion. (2) The record is a list [dev, ino], so the adapter to a mapping must check length and exact int types; compare_identity already rejects bool and negative values (probed). (3) Pre-existing and out of scope: a same-device bind mount inside the area passes the st_dev check in _empty_directory and would be traversed; it needs root to create. Unverified: no Linux, WSL2 or overlay/NFS execution; the cross-platform claim rests on simulated drift, as the plan says.
proposition: security-reviewer approves the current affected scope
safety_and_authorization: Local review evidence only; no external side effects.

observed: Plan is architecturally sound. Reusing storage_identity.compare_identity inside _read_owner fits the helper contract: the owner record's directory identity is a persisted cross-run identity compared against a live fstat, and the caller already owns locator/role validation (key from the resolved wave record via _target, every component pinned by the O_NOFOLLOW dir_fd walk in _parent, plus owner repository==str(resolved root), wave, schema and generation checks, then _anchor/_entry re-verification). That is stronger locator validation than the 1yja8 callers (publication_control, sqlite_storage_migration use same_path + compare_identity). No restamping and unchanged record format match 1yja8. Within-run checks (_same, _entry, _anchor, _parent identities) stay strict, correct since they compare stats taken in one operation. Native Windows claim verified: _SAFE_DELETE requires os.open in os.supports_dir_fd (empty on nt), so _parent and cleanup_work refuse with safe_work_io_unsupported before any ownership read. Probe: compare_identity on real 21s7b values returns matches/path+inode/device_drift; inode mismatch and bool-typed device return no-match/invalid. Docs scope: threat-model sentence is the right home; data-and-control-flow.md:282, domain-map.md:15/79 and mcp-tool-surface.md:1589 describe parent/directory identity checks only generically and stay accurate (inode still bound), so no update required. Non-blocking notes for implementation: (1) the record stores directory as a list [dev, ino]; conversion to the helper's {device, inode} mapping must reject non-list, wrong length and non-int/bool values as malformed. (2) compare_identity treats a zero inode on either side as path-only basis (probe: stored inode 0 matches any live inode); _read_owner should refuse a stored or live inode of 0 so the inode binding cannot be dropped by a zeroed record, and AC-3's malformed case should include it. (3) Change doc says five callers but lists four functions / six call sites (grep: 7 occurrences including def); wording only. (4) The persisted-identity guard allow-list for wave_work must also cover _empty_directory's within-operation info.st_dev != os.fstat(fd).st_dev mount-crossing check and _parent/_anchor identity lists, not just _same/_entry/_anchor named in Requirement 3.
